verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly documents its own event-driven automation in release contexts. Guarded rollouts watch selected metrics and progress or halt traffic on their own, and Autopilot claims automatic rollback when something breaks. There is also an 'Adaptive triggers' heading, but no content behind it. Scheduled changes are time-based rather than event-based, so they do not count. Missing for 10: a documented general-purpose way for users to define event-to-action rules, details on trigger types and configuration beyond the bare 'Adaptive triggers' title, a documented rollback-on-regression mechanism beyond marketing copy, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: A guarded rollout progressively increases traffic to the new variation while monitoring selected metrics for regressions until the rollout reaches 100%.
Autopilot ships it safely, and rolls it back if it breaks.
